verdicts.note: Union dissolution among women evaluated for fertility problems.

**NEJM: Connecticut and Rhode Island MANDATE COVERAGE FOR FERTILITY PRESERVATION.** A P1-shaped exposure landing inside Wall 5's population — and the indication is not named in the abstract, so it is also a residue case. If preservation mandates spread, P5 acquires the policy variation it currently lacks entirely.
Marital stability after unsuccessful treatment.
Age and ART success rates, retrospective.

Fertility treatment use among US women WITH LIVEBORN INFANTS, 1997-2004, covering ART AND NON-ART. Births as the denominator and the non-ART share included — the two things the ART registries cannot give arm 1 on their own.
Theory-of-planned-behaviour test of intentions to DELAY. On P6's mechanism, but intentions only.
No abstract. Maternal self-report of ART use versus registry data — measurement validity for the exposure series.

**Technology DIFFUSION and MARKET STRUCTURE in infertility treatment markets.** The supply-side entry margin with an economics design. P2's set is now: proximity, competition, chain ownership, market structure, legal eligibility, and rationing rules.
Cryopreservation's contribution to the CUMULATIVE LIVE BIRTH RATE, Italian registry. Arm-1 shape, per-cycle denominator — Wall 1 by outcome.
Regional subfertility incidence, Netherlands.
Maternal age and offspring education.
Australian community approval of IVF across THREE DECADES of surveys. Attitudes to the technology, tracked long enough to show acceptance rising alongside uptake.
Students' knowledge of ELECTIVE oocyte cryopreservation.

**'CAN REPEAT IVF/ICSI CYCLES COMPENSATE FOR THE NATURAL DECLINE IN FERTILITY WITH AGE?' — Leridon's question, asked again on 4,102 Chinese women over 35 with cumulative live-birth rates.** An empirical answer to the modelling question P4's anchor posed. The outcome is per-cycle-cumulative rather than population, so extraction must convert carefully — but this is the direct test.
Mental health around first birth by conception mode.
Previous caesarean and IVF live-birth rates.
Longer AWARENESS of ART fosters positive attitudes and acceptance. The belief channel's dynamic form — familiarity raising confidence in the technology.
PRAMS ART-use question validation. Measurement provenance.
Men's first-childbearing timing decisions.
Japan's declining birth rate and policy, overview.
Indonesian residents' preservation knowledge.
A record titled 'Introduction'. Paratext — the fifth in this screen.
Hope and fantasy in coping with infertility.
Donor sperm after repeated implantation failure.
Mean age at birth in Ukraine.
Advanced maternal age in Ukraine.
Commentary on infertility as a disease category. Bears on whether coverage mandates are framed as medical necessity.
Portuguese women's fertility and preservation knowledge.
Israel's reproductive law and policy. The institutional context for the free-IVF natural experiment, and evidence on why Israel's transportability is limited.
Contraceptive use and time to first birth. A.2's.
Ambient temperature and fecundity in 2.4 million couples. B's, and large.
German dissertation on treating patients over 40.
Spatial educational gradient of first motherhood, Spain.
Infertility prevalence, Burkina Faso. Walls 4 and 8.
AMH as an ovarian-function marker.

Economic Modelling 2026: age- and parity-specific Australian birth trends and whether low fertility is inevitable. Parity-specific is the decomposition arm 1 needs; whether ART enters the model is not visible.
Wellbeing when facing a blocked parenthood goal.
IVF twins' contribution to the preterm rate over 25 years. A.12 by exposure, Wall 2 by outcome.
Emotional adjustment to IVF, review.
ANZARD 2007 — the Australia/New Zealand series named in the scope's exposure list, now present in the frame.
Systematic review of infertility prevalence definitions. Wall 4's measurement problem.
**Systematic review of WORLDWIDE ART TRENDS 2004-2013.** A single synthesised source for the cross-national utilisation series — a channel-1 record for the demographic-significance stage.
Semen parameters and time to pregnancy.
Child penalty in adopting and same-sex couples. Uses ADOPTION as the comparison — methodologically adjacent to the ART-adoption substitution question.
Nation-wide frequency of INVOLUNTARY infertility, estimated without excluding couples who remain infertile. Wall 4, but it is the cleanest estimate of the population A.17 is about.
Age-related versus unexplained infertility. The diagnostic boundary that decides whether ART is treating an age effect or something else.
Feminist perspectives on reproduction.

**HOUSEHOLD INCOME and medical help-seeking for fertility problems, representative Japanese population.** Income gradients in treatment entry are the reduced form of the price mechanism arm 2 estimates from policy — and Japan is a setting with its own subsidy regime.
Demographics of a US public-hospital infertility population.
Academic performance after frozen embryo transfer.
eHealth literacy for infertility.
Night-shift work and reproductive outcomes.
Adolescent oncofertility counselling ethics.

**Probability of a SECOND live birth after a first NATURAL versus MAR-mediated birth, historical cohort.** Parity progression conditional on how the first birth was achieved — the mechanism by which ART's contribution to completed fertility differs from its contribution to first births. Lazzari's parity-transition question with a comparison group.
Students' and professors' preservation awareness.
Men's childbearing preferences, dissertation.
AMH versus other ovarian-reserve metrics.
Emotional distress by partner sex.
Commentary on demand for pregnancy at advanced age.
Spanish legal working age and family behaviour. C.3.b's.
